source_text: Ἀπηγγέλθη δέ τι ἡμῖν καὶ ἄπιστον ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ ὑμῶν γενόμενον, πάντως που ὑπὸ ἀπίστων καὶ ἀσεβῶν καὶ μὴ εἰδότων μηδὲ ὄνομα Κυρίου· ὅτι ἄρα εἰς τοσοῦτόν τινες ὠμότητος καὶ ἀπανθρωπίας προεχώρησαν, ὥστε τινὰς τοὺς διαφυγόντας αἰχμαλώτους βίᾳ κατέχειν. Ἀποστείλατέ τινας εἰς τὴν χώραν, μὴ καὶ σκηπτοὶ πέσωσιν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας.
thought_title: Report of captives held by force and call for intervention
orientation: Gregory reports hearing that some escaped captives are being violently detained in the addressee's region by unbelievers, and urges sending people to intervene before the perpetrators fall into a trap.
pass_a_gloss: Something was reported to us also, unbelievable, having occurred in your region, surely by unbelievers and impious ones and ones not knowing even the name of the Lord; that some proceeded to so great a degree of savagery and inhumanity, so as to hold by force some captives who had escaped. Send some people into the region, lest also the perpetrators of such things fall into a snare.

choices.why: The glossary prefers literal senses; 'unbelievable' captures the predicate adjective modifying the reported event without importing 'incredible' as a judgment of truth-value.
The particle combination expresses confident inference about agency; 'surely' conveys the epistemic force in one word rather than a periphrasis.
Both nouns denote extreme moral depravity; 'savagery' matches ὠμότης (brutality) and 'inhumanity' matches ἀπανθρωπία (lack of human feeling) without collapsing them into a single idea.
σκηπτός is a verbal adjective from σκάπτω (to dig a pit/trap); 'fall into a snare' preserves the passive sense of being caught in a trap set by their own actions, not merely 'be trapped'.
πράσσω implies habitual or deliberate practice; 'doing such things' keeps the generality and agency, while 'perpetrating' would narrow it to crimes only.

pass_b_english: Something unbelievable has been reported to us as having been done in your region — surely by unbelievers, godless people who do not even know the name of the Lord. Some have advanced to such a degree of savagery and inhumanity that they are holding by force certain captives who had escaped. Send some people into the region, lest thunderbolts fall upon those who do such things.

problems.quote: lest they too fall into a snare against those doing such things
problems.source_quote: μὴ καὶ σκηπτοὶ πέσωσιν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας
problems.why: σκηπτοί means thunderbolts, and they are the subject of πέσωσιν: thunderbolts fall on the wrongdoers. The English adds a 'snare', makes the envoys the subject, and is incoherent.
problems.fix: Send some people into the region, lest thunderbolts fall upon those who do such things.

problems.quote: lest they too fall into a snare against those doing such things
problems.source_quote: μὴ καὶ σκηπτοὶ πέσωσιν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας
problems.why: 'Fall into a snare against those doing such things' makes no sense, and 'they' could be the envoys or the wrongdoers.
problems.fix: Send some people into the region, lest thunderbolts fall upon those who do such things.
problems.ruling: English 'they' drops σκηπτοί (rulers); πέσωσιν ἐπί is fall upon, not snare—agents and action mislead readers.

edits.old: lest they too fall into a snare against those doing such things
edits.new: lest thunderbolts fall upon those who do such things

fixed: mistranslation: fixed — μὴ καὶ σκηπτοὶ πέσωσιν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας has σκηπτοὶ (thunderbolts) as subject of πέσωσιν falling upon the wrongdoers, not envoys falling into a snare.
unreadable: fixed by same edit — replaces incoherent 'fall into a snare against those doing such things' with subject-verb-object that fits the sentence.

problems.quote: has been reported to us as having happened in your region — surely by unbelievers
problems.source_quote: ἄπιστον ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ ὑμῶν γενόμενον, πάντως που ὑπὸ ἀπίστων καὶ ἀσεβῶν
problems.why: In the Greek, 'by unbelievers' goes with the deed being done, not with the report. The English could be read as saying that unbelievers made the report.
problems.fix: We have been told of something unbelievable done in your region, surely the work of unbelievers, godless people who do not even know the name of the Lord.
problems.ruling: Ὑπὸ ἀπίστων attaches to γενόμενον, not Ἀπηγγέλθη; English dash can imply unbelievers made the report.

edits.old: as having happened in your region — surely by unbelievers
edits.new: as having been done in your region — surely by unbelievers

fixed: agency is real: ὑπὸ ἀπίστων goes with γενόμενον, but intransitive `happened ... by unbelievers` attached `by` to `reported`; changed to `been done ... by` to attach agency to the deed.
